setup_note: The first run exposed a spec/evaluator mismatch: redis-py's decr() path used DECRBY, while the spec named DECR but not DECRBY. The spec and evaluator were corrected, then fresh builders were run.

evaluator_only_run.interpretation: This is not a product-spec condition. It measures whether a builder can implement to the tests when the evaluator is visible.

leakage_audit.obvious_forbidden_string_scan: no hits for evaluator/result/prior-solution markers in corrected servers
leakage_audit.isolation_limit: Workers saw temp spec copies and output paths, but the evaluator still existed in the parent repo. This is not a formally sandboxed blind eval.

interpretation: A more complex Redis-like server target still did not separate final behavior between clean and minimum-implied specs on one builder each.
The minimum-implied spec was about 46 percent shorter by word count, but its implementation was longer: 727 lines versus 645 lines.
The evaluator-only condition also passed and produced the shortest implementation, 462 lines, which suggests visible tests can serve as a very compact target but invite overfitting.
This supports the emerging pattern: strong builders recover behavior when enough facts are present, while spec quality shows up more reliably as process cost.
